cards.b: 50 marks (AO2): two parts, solo and with others; 30% of the IGCSE.
50 marks (AO3): two compositions, 25 each; 30% of the IGCSE.
At least 2 minutes per part; no more than 10 minutes in total.
Final recording of each piece must be a single take, not edited.
Rhythmic coordination and ensemble awareness with at least one live performer.
Fluency/accuracy; tempo/coordination; character/style/ensemble; technical control; whole performance.
Notated in staff notation as a complete score, with a recording.
Written to your own brief linked to an area of study; recording plus commentary or suitable score.
Ideas, structure, use of medium, compositional technique, score or commentary.
Suitable writing for instruments, ranges and a variety of textures.
Developing ideas (sequence, inversion, ostinato) with suitable harmony.
Arrangements of existing pieces; theme and variations on someone else's theme.
Brief, timings, structure and content, how effects were made.
A pattern repeated higher or lower.
Listening, balancing dynamics and matching phrasing with other performers.

short.q: How does the Cambridge syllabus judge the difficulty of a performing piece?
short.model: Marks are for the skills shown, not for difficulty, but very simple pieces limit marks and pieces that are too hard cause errors.
It follows your own brief linked to an area of study, and comes with a recording plus a commentary or style-appropriate notation; it must use different instruments from Composition 1.
Listening to other performers, balancing dynamics and matching phrasing and articulation.

short.q: How can you improve the structure of a composition?
short.model: Plan sections with contrast and links, use repetition and variation, and keep an overall shape with a clear ending.

short.q: What should a composition commentary include?
short.model: The brief, timings, the structure and content of each section and how effects were achieved (instruments, devices, keys, technology).
